VeraGrid.Gui.Diagrams.SchematicWidget.schematic_auto_layout.apply_initial_auto_layout_to_diagram(diagram: SchematicDiagram, layout_name: str = 'power_system_layout', position_scale: float = 500.0) → None[source]

Apply one automatic layout directly to the stored diagram coordinates.

This function operates only on the persisted GraphicLocation records and does not require any Qt graphics objects to exist yet. Running it before scene creation avoids the expensive transient state where all node widgets are initially stacked at the origin.

Parameters:

  • diagram – Schematic diagram to modify.

  • layout_name – Automatic layout mode to evaluate.

  • position_scale – Final coordinate scaling factor in pixels.

Returns:

None.

The algorithm combines three stages: 1. dominant electrical-backbone extraction with a spanning tree, 2. rooted tree placement using subtree spans, 3. constrained spring-like vertical refinement with fixed tree-depth columns.

  • graph – Diagram graph with electrical metadata.

VeraGrid.Gui.Diagrams.SchematicWidget.schematic_auto_layout.get_layout_edge_max_compact_distance(edge_data: Dict[str, Any], base_radius_gap: float) → float[source]

The target distance is intentionally much smaller than the normal radial gap. This keeps buses linked through 2-winding transformers or the winding spokes of 3-winding and N-winding transformers from spreading apart as the radial sectors expand.

  • base_radius_gap – Base radial step used for line-like edges.

Maximum preferred Euclidean edge length in layout units.

  • from_idx – Source node index.

  • to_idx – Target node index.

Representative edge metadata dictionary.

Transformer-like couplings do not represent corridor distance. They represent a tight electrical relationship around the same station area, so the connected node symbols should remain visually close.

edge_device_tpe – Edge device type.

Returns:

True when the edge should be compacted strongly.

VeraGrid.Gui.Diagrams.SchematicWidget.schematic_auto_layout.refine_positions_for_transformer_compactness(component_graph: Graph | MultiGraph, positions: Dict[int, ndarray], base_radius_gap: float, iteration_count: int = 14, blend_factor: float = 0.32) → Dict[int, ndarray][source]

Contract transformer-linked nodes after the coarse radial placement.

The radial tree placement decides the global spider-web geometry, but it can still leave transformer-connected nodes too far apart because their angular sectors may widen with the surrounding subtree. This refinement only contracts compact transformer edges and leaves line corridors untouched.

Parameters:

  • component_graph – Connected component graph.

  • positions – Initial node positions for the component.

  • base_radius_gap – Base radial step used for line-like edges.

  • iteration_count – Number of contraction iterations.

  • blend_factor – Fraction of the excess edge length corrected per iteration.

Returns:

Refined component positions.

VeraGrid.Gui.Diagrams.SchematicWidget.schematic_auto_layout.should_auto_layout_before_first_draw(diagram: SchematicDiagram, epsilon: float = 1e-06) → bool[source]

Determine whether the schematic should be auto-laid out before any graphics are created.

The check intentionally looks only at visible bus-like anchors. If every visible anchor is still at the origin, drawing all widgets first would stack them at the same scene position and make Qt spend time resolving a pathological geometry state.

Parameters:

  • diagram – Schematic diagram to inspect.

  • epsilon – Tolerance used to compare coordinates against the origin.

Returns:

True when an initial auto-layout should run before drawing.

class VeraGrid.Gui.Diagrams.SchematicWidget.schematic_widget.SchematicWidget(gui: VeraGridMainGUI | DiagramsMain, diagram: SchematicDiagram, default_bus_voltage: float = 10.0, time_index: None | int = None)[source]

Bases: BaseDiagramWidget

This is the bus-branch editor

Structure:

{SchematicWidget: BaseDiagramWidget}
- .editor_graphics_view {QGraphicsView} (Handles the drag and drop)
- .diagram_scene {SchematicScene: QGraphicsScene}
- .circuit {MultiCircuit} (Calculation engine)
- .diagram {SchematicDiagram} records the DB objects and their position to load and save diagrams
- .graphics_manager {GraphicsManager} records the DB objects and their diagram widgets

The graphic objects need to call the API objects and functions inside the MultiCircuit instance. To do this the graphic objects call “parent.circuit.<function or object>”

get_wheel_zoom_steps(event: QWheelEvent) → float[source]

Convert a wheel event into a normalized zoom step count.

A mouse wheel commonly emits an angle delta of 120 units per notch, while laptop touchpads emit many smaller high-resolution events and may provide pixel deltas. Normalizing by the event magnitude keeps mouse-wheel zoom unchanged and makes touchpad zoom proportional to the gesture instead of applying one full zoom step per event.

Parameters:

event – Wheel event coming from the graphics view.

Returns:

Signed zoom step count.

schedule_branch_callbacks_after_draw() → None[source]

Coalesce expensive post-draw branch refresh work into a single pass.

During initial startup, draw() can run before the widget is shown. In that case we must defer the refresh until showEvent(). Once the widget is visible, repeated draw/update paths should still collapse into one queued refresh instead of replaying the full callback and redraw sweep multiple times.

Returns:

None.

reassign_terminal(graphic_obj: LineGraphicTemplateItem, another_terminal: BaseTerminal) → None[source]

Reassign one branch graphic from another terminal to this one.

The branch graphic must update its endpoint port reference as well as the callback registration. Otherwise deleting the old host graphic leaves the branch visually attached to a dead terminal object.

Parameters:

  • graphic_obj – Branch graphic being moved.

  • another_terminal – Previously attached terminal.
